$comment: technical.rsi_14@1.0.0 — source §8.7, simple-mean RSI(14) (see the method's own doc comment for why simple mean rather than Wilder smoothing). Every case hand-computed.

abstention.message: The price series is tagged 'intraday', not 'adjusted_close'.

cases.name: all_up_no_losses
cases.why: 14 consecutive +1 sessions, no losing session: avg_loss = 0, RSI = 100 by the divide-by-zero guard — a clamp, marked with a warning (lane-review, round 3).

warnings: No losing session in the window, so avg_loss is zero. RSI(14) is reported as 100 — the formula's ceiling — rather than dividing by zero.

cases.name: all_down_no_gains
cases.why: 14 consecutive −1 sessions: avg_gain = 0, avg_loss = 1, RS = 0, RSI = 100 − 100/(1+0) = 0.

cases.name: flat_neutral
cases.why: 15 identical closes: avg_gain = avg_loss = 0, reported as the conventional neutral reading, 50, not an abstention — a clamp, marked with a warning (lane-review, round 3).

warnings: Every close in the window is identical — no gains and no losses — so RSI(14) is reported as the conventional neutral reading, 50, rather than computed.

cases.name: mixed_rs_three
cases.why: Two +21 sessions then one −14 session, 11 flat sessions: sum_gains = 42, sum_losses = 14 over 14 changes — avg_gain = 3 and avg_loss = 1 both land on whole numbers (not repeating decimals, unlike a naive +6/−2 choice), so RS = 3 exactly and RSI = 100 − 100/(1+3) = 75 exactly.
